final_answer: Accept all seven decision atoms; reject none. The four consensus code/config atoms fully satisfy the task's success tests and are low-risk: (1) set the committed default to yolo11m in configs/live-webcam.yaml via model_file/model_size, not hardcoded; (2) keep the model selectable via config/CLI with no hardcoded model path in UltralyticsDetector or its loader; (3) add conf_threshold: float = 0.4 to the DetectorConfig schema; (4) actually pass that conf_threshold into the Ultralytics inference call, fixing the parameter being dropped in the factory. The unit-test atom is accepted because it cheaply locks the new config-to-inference path. The two execution atoms are accepted WITH the judge's modifications folded in: the yolo11x demo runs exactly once on device 0 through a temporary, uncommitted override (CLI flag) — never by editing the committed default — and must explicitly handle the case where the physical camera or the yolo11x weights are unavailable (fail loudly with a documented reason, do not fake the frame); and the output must be two concrete artifacts, the annotated runs/webcam-proof-v2.png plus a structured runs/webcam-proof-v2.json log carrying the required fields (class, confidence, bbox, model, device, timestamp/latency) mirroring the existing webcam-proof-capture.json format. Net deliverable: balanced yolo11m default + working conf_threshold=0.4 wiring + a fresh real-camera yolo11x proof frame and its detection log.

decisions.decision: Set yolo11m as the committed default in configs/live-webcam.yaml (model_file: models/yolo11m.pt, model_size: m, model_family: yolo), not hardcoded.
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.895, full proposal consensus (A/B/C). yolo11m is the stated FPS/accuracy balance for continuous cameras and directly satisfies success test #1 while leaving the value override-able.
alternatives_considered: Keep yolo11x as default (rejected by user feedback)
Leave default unset/inherited (fails the explicit-default success test)
decisions.test: configs/live-webcam.yaml contains model_file: models/yolo11m.pt (or equivalent); loading with no override resolves to yolo11m.

decisions.decision: Keep model selection driven entirely by config/CLI override; remove or confirm-absent any hardcoded model path (e.g. yolo11x.pt) in UltralyticsDetector and its loading path.
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.875. Prevents brittle hardcoded selection and preserves runtime override — the core constraint of the task ('model must remain configurable', 'do not hardcode yolo11x').
alternatives_considered: Branch on a hardcoded constant in code (violates constraint)
Env-var-only selection (less discoverable than config + CLI)

Per-call argument only without schema field — fails the schema success test

decisions.decision: Pass conf_threshold from DetectorConfig into the Ultralytics inference call (conf=...) in UltralyticsDetector, fixing the parameter being dropped in factory.py (~line 26).

decisions.decision: [MODIFIED] Run yolo11x exactly once on device 0 via a temporary, uncommitted override (CLI flag, e.g. --model models/yolo11x.pt), NOT by editing the committed default; explicitly handle camera/model-unavailability by failing loudly with a documented reason rather than fabricating output.

red_team_findings.what: Switching the committed default to model_file: models/yolo11m.pt will make the default live runner FAIL its readiness gate, because that weight is not vendored (only models/yolov8n.pt exists on disk).
red_team_findings.why: LiveReadinessChecker._detector_issues (src/oko/live/readiness.py:176-185) emits a 'blocker' (detector_model_file_not_found) when config.detector.model_file is not an existing file. webcam.py:36-39 calls this before running and returns exit 2 with {"ok": false} if any blocker exists. So `python -m oko.live.webcam` against the new default would never run — it fails preflight. This is a regression versus the current yolov8n.pt default, and success_test #1 ('system loads yolo11m by default') fails at the gate before any load. The decision/open_questions only flag downloading yolo11x.pt; they never flag that the new committed DEFAULT (yolo11m.pt) must also be vendored or downloaded, which requires network. Implementation_plan step 10 ('verify config still resolves to yolo11m') would pass on config text but the runner is broken.

red_team_findings.what: The committed real-run evidence shows device 0 in this environment yields a near-unusable feed and only sub-0.4 false positives — combined with the new conf_threshold=0.4 default and the 'run once' constraint, the yolo11x proof is likely to produce an empty/garbage frame that fails the goal, with no allowed retry.
red_team_findings.why: runs/webcam-proof-capture.json records 60 frames attempted but only 2 read, and the single detection was 'surfboard' @0.2832. runs/webcam-real-run.txt shows 'surfboard'@0.3 and 'person'@0.3. Every one of those confidences is below 0.4, so the new default threshold filters them to ZERO detections. The decision frames camera risk as binary (available vs unavailable) and plans only for clean unavailability; the evidenced failure mode is 'available-but-garbage feed yielding sub-threshold/false detections', which it does not plan for. Because the demo must run exactly once (constraint), a poor/empty first frame cannot be retried without violating the constraint — a catch-22 between failing the goal ('good recognition quality' / success_test #5: a real detection result) and violating 'perform only once'. The decision's 'documented failure' escape produces an artifact that explicitly fails success_test #5.

red_team_findings.what: Adding conf_threshold default 0.4 and forwarding it from the factory silently raises the effective threshold from 0.25 to 0.4 for ALL ultralytics configs, not just live-webcam.
red_team_findings.why: UltralyticsDetector currently defaults confidence=0.25 (ultralytics_detector.py:23) and already passes conf=self.confidence to predict (line 47). The wiring gap is only that build_detector (factory.py:26) constructs UltralyticsDetector(model_file=...) without forwarding confidence. Once the factory forwards config.conf_threshold (default 0.4), example.yaml and live-template.yaml — which also use provider: ultralytics — inherit 0.4 because they don't set the field. This is a behavior change beyond live-webcam: detections in the 0.25–0.40 band (exactly where the prior real run lived) disappear. It is not scoped, called out, or regression-tested as a global change.

red_team_findings.what: The 'temporary CLI-flag override' path for the yolo11x demo does not exist, and no committed entrypoint produces the required annotated PNG + structured JSON — that tooling is ad-hoc/external and must be (re)written.
red_team_findings.why: The webcam runner exposes only --config/--rules/--mode/--frames/--camera-id/--project-root (webcam.py:24-29); there is no --model or --conf flag. All three entrypoints (webcam/runtime/smoke) run the full pipeline and print bridge JSON — none call imwrite or emit a detection-capture JSON. The existing runs/webcam-proof.png + webcam-proof-capture.json were produced by ad-hoc code not present in src/. So the proof run requires writing a one-off capture script (added scope vs allowed_complexity 'low'), and an 'ephemeral yolo11x config' run through webcam.py would still trip the same readiness blocker (readiness.py:177) unless yolo11x.pt is downloaded first. Open_question #3 (CLI flag vs ephemeral config) is left unresolved while the CLI-flag option is not actually available.

red_team_findings.what: The proof step depends on TWO network downloads (yolo11x.pt ~109MB AND the new default yolo11m.pt), both gated by the same readiness blocker if absent; the decision only anticipates one.
red_team_findings.why: open_questions only asks whether models/yolo11x.pt is present. But the committed default now needs models/yolo11m.pt too, and readiness.py:177 blocks the runner for any missing weight. If the environment is offline (plausible for an automated agent run), both the default config and the proof run are dead on arrival. The decision's graceful-failure plan covers camera/GPU but not weight-download failure for the default model.

red_team_findings.what: model_family and model_size are dead metadata; setting model_size: m is cosmetic and only model_file actually selects the model.
red_team_findings.why: grep confirms model_family/model_size appear nowhere except their schema.py definitions (lines 12-13); build_detector (factory.py:26) loads strictly from config.model_file. The decision sets model_size: m and model_family: yolo alongside model_file, which is harmless but creates a foot-gun: a future maintainer changing model_size will not change the loaded model. Only the model_file edit is load-bearing for success_test #1.

red_team_findings.what: Naming mismatch and factory branch hazard: DetectorConfig.conf_threshold maps to the detector's existing 'confidence' param, and the fake-detector branch must not receive the new kwarg.
red_team_findings.why: The decision describes 'fix factory parameter-dropping' and 'wire conf= to predict', but predict already receives conf=self.confidence (ultralytics_detector.py:47) and nothing is currently 'dropped' (conf_threshold doesn't exist yet). The real one-line fix is factory.py:26 forwarding config.conf_threshold into UltralyticsDetector(confidence=...). Also, the fake branch (factory.py:24) calls FakeDetector(model_file=..., **kwargs); if conf_threshold is threaded naively it could be passed to a provider that doesn't accept it. Success_test #4 still passes by value-flow, but the conf_threshold vs confidence name divergence is left unreconciled.

red_team_findings.what: Self-contradictory output-format spec: 'mirror the existing webcam-proof-capture.json format' conflicts with the new fields the decision lists.
red_team_findings.why: runs/webcam-proof-capture.json uses keys label/box_xyxy/model_file/confidence_threshold and has no model/device/latency/bbox/class keys. The decision simultaneously says mirror that format and emit class/confidence/bbox/model/device/latency. These cannot both hold; the implementer must choose, and success_test #6 specifically requires class+confidence per detection — using 'label' (as the existing file does) would technically diverge from 'class'.
